passages.heading: United Nations Convention On The Rights Of Persons With Disabilities
passages.text: The United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UNCRPD) is an international human rights treaty of the United Nations intended to protect the rights and dignity of persons with disabilities.

passages.heading: United Nations Convention On The Rights Of Persons With Disabilities
passages.text: It aims to ensure that persons with disabilities enjoy the same human rights as everyone else and that they can participate fully in society by receiving the same opportunities as others.

passages.heading: United Nations Convention On The Rights Of Persons With Disabilities
passages.text: Image: Map Of Bangladesh 8 Division: Dhaka, Chittagong, Khulna, Rajshahi, Sylhet, Barishal, Rangpur, Mymensingh Bangladesh is one of 181 states that have ratified the UNCRPD

passages.heading: United Nations Convention On The Rights Of Persons With Disabilities
passages.text: By ratifying the UNCRPD, Bangladesh is committed to promoting and protecting the full enjoyment of human rights by persons with disabilities and ensuring they have full equality under the law.

passages.heading: United Nations Convention On The Rights Of Persons With Disabilities
passages.text: The Convention covers a wide range of areas including, education, employment, access to justice, personal security, independent living, and access to information.

passages.heading: Recommendations
passages.text: Recommendations

passages.heading: Recommendations
passages.text: More focus should be given towards ensuring the standard AAAQ (accessibility, availability, acceptability and quality) framework while delivering services and interventions related to SRHR of persons with disabilities

passages.heading: Recommendations
passages.text: Age appropriate comprehensive sexuality education should be taught in all special schools and in technical and vocational training institutes in the country

passages.heading: Recommendations
passages.text: Government should focus on reducing social stigma and misconception around SRHR of persons with disabilities

passages.heading: Recommendations
passages.text: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare may take the initiative of providing free sanitary napkins to adolescent girls with disabilities in urban and rural areas

passages.heading: Recommendations
passages.text: More awareness programs are required to prevent violence against persons with disabilities, especially the emotional abuse faced by persons with developmental disabilities

passages.heading: Recommendations
passages.text: Institutional responses of different government departments need to be strengthened to address any kind of discrimination and abuse against persons with disabilities

passages.heading: Recommendations
passages.text: Appropriate interventions and plans are required for providing legal support to the sexually assaulted victims.

passages.heading: Recommendations
passages.text: Capacity building of different official (such as, health care providers, police personnel and practicing lawyers) should be considered a priority

passages.heading: Recommendations
passages.text: Multisectoral collaboration among different ministries (e.g., Ministry of Social Welfare, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare etc.) and other stakeholders (e.g., NGOs, INGOs, DPOs, developmental partners and civil society) needs to be strengthened in other to meet the SDGs related to disability and SRHR and in ensuring the rights of persons with disabilities as per the UNCRPD
